grader.call_summary: Nightly full outages traced to a loose, uncapped splitter knocked by painters. Splitter removed, signal verified, speed test on wired PC, 48-hour line monitor set. Solid call with two misses: two repeated questions and a casual close without the S-Net closing script or survey.
grader.criteria_source: resources/criteria_config.json (tenant-abc): 11 items, weights Soft Skills 0.333 / Technical Knowledge 0.667
app_traps: Announced hold with check-ins counted as dead air
Reworded repeat questions slip under the 0.70 similarity pre-filter

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Opening is correct at [00:00], but the close at [17:25] is 'Thanks for calling S-Net, have a great night' with no 'Thank you for choosing S-Net' and no survey invitation.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: Hold done by the book: [03:23] asks permission and states the duration, [04:52] checks back after ~50 s, [05:56] thanks the customer for waiting. Announced holds with check-ins are not dead air.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Rule: FAIL (likely false). The rule treats each turn as 10 s long and counts both hold segments (47 s, 40 s) as dead air; it cannot see that the hold was announced.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: [00:18] account number and PIN, [00:34] name on the account, [00:42] 'you're verified'.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [00:18] 'I'm sorry to hear that'; [12:21] 'I understand, that's really frustrating, especially when you were told to just wait it out' in reply to the late-shift complaint.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides. The real frustration moment is skipped by the keyword filter (agent said 'understand'/'frustrating'), so Laya is shown two neutral problem-description turns (00:48, 01:47) that were picked only because of sentiment drops. Outcome uncertain.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [01:09] 'So just to make sure I've got it: most evenings the whole connection drops out, for anywhere from two to five minutes, three or four times a night...'

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Re-asks two things already answered: [06:27] 'how long has this been happening for, roughly?' (answered at [01:36]) -> customer: 'Like I said, about three weeks'; [13:31] 'Does it happen on your wired devices as well?' (answered at [01:47]) -> 'Yeah, I mentioned the gaming PC drops too.'
items.expected_app_behaviour: Rule: PASS (likely false). Both repeats are reworded, so no question pair reaches the 0.70 similarity needed to send them to Laya.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: Finds the cause herself, sets a 48-hour monitor at [14:51] ('we'll contact you, so you won't need to call in again'), explains the free technician fallback.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: [01:31] duration, [01:39] wired vs WiFi, [01:58] modem lights, [02:41] time-of-day pattern, [03:00] recent changes, [08:15] whether painters moved the cabinet.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides; real diagnostic questions do reach it here.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [16:41] 'can you confirm everything is working for you now?' -> 'Yeah, it's been solid' -> [16:55] 'I'm happy we've resolved it tonight'.
